HydroCraft KDT · Calibration Framework · v2

Calibration, made honest and general.

A standalone parameter-calibration system for 400+ Earth-system model KIs. The KI runs the model, the literature grounds every choice, and no result is trusted until it proves it generalizes — and until it proves the parameters actually reached the run.

foundation 1 The KI is the execution backbone
foundation 2 The literature is the grounding
invariant parameters never promote to the KI
01

The pipeline

One run of calibrate.py, gate to gate.
calibrate.py --model X --case Y
gate 1 · readiness
Has self-improve validated that this model runs correctly?
Reads self_improve_runs for a valid_case. Calibration only tunes values, and assumes the model + setup are already sound.
no valid_case
skip & record “not ready”
yes
carry case_id · determining_metric · prior_metric
capability-dev · once, if missing
Author the KI's calibration capability
An agent writes calibration.yaml (literature-grounded params, ranges, priors, holdout, provenance) + tools/calib_run.py — a thin wrapper over the KI's own run tools.
the engine · calibration_kit model-agnostic — 7–8 optimizers, one execution path
1 · Sensitivity screen — Morris, literature-seeded
Papers name the sensitive params; a cheap residual screen confirms on this site's data. Literature is a prior, never a pruning oracle.
2 · optimize loop  ↻  until budget / convergence
propose
optimizer emits a param vector DDS · NSGA-II · BoTorch
→
inject
value into the model's inputs applicator · or · runner
→
run
the KI's own run tools execute in the eval workdir
→
score
gate-valid metrics → loss back to the optimizer
gate 2 · holdout
Do the best params generalize, or just overfit the calibration set?
Re-score on a held-out split whose protocol + generalization_axis follow the field (blocked-temporal · leave-region-out · blocked space-time).
fail
record holdout_fail · not applied
pass
proceed to case-apply
case-apply
Best params → case_params/<case>.json
Never written into the KI. Calibrated values are per-site; only the capability is KI-promotable, and that's self-improve's job.
record
One calibration_runs row
Lifecycle and science kept separate, as DB CHECK constraints — a run can complete and still be a scientific failure.
02

Injection — how a value reaches the model

Per-KI mode. Generic formats are central; model-specific files are delegated.

applicator the default, verified path

The kit writes each value into a stable input file by its declared address, and proves it with a read-after-write round-trip (C7). One handler, reused across many models.

yaml_pathjson_pathini_key text_tokennamelistfixed_width table_cell

runner the general escape hatch

The kit hands calib_run.py the vector via KDT_CALIB_PARAMS; the KI injects it the model's own way. Required when inputs are regenerated each run, or live in a model-specific format.

flopy → modflow_pkgpyswmm → swmm_inp apino central handler

The distinction is level, not preference: a format (namelist, fixed-width) is one reusable handler; a model (MODFLOW packages, SWMM decks) needs its native library — a central handler would just reimplement flopy.

03

Runner mode proves itself twice

Delegated injection is only trusted when it can't silently do nothing.
every evaluation

Round-trip · did the write happen?

The runner echoes __kdt__.applied_params; the kit diffs it against the request on every eval — exact keyset, non-finite rejected, no clamp-to-zero. Any mismatch scores the run +inf.

◆ fail-closed — a non-injecting runner is never trusted
once · commissioning

Responsiveness · did the run consume it?

Before optimizing, perturb each param to the far bound (so even a bool or small int actually changes). If no perturbation moves any objective, the params aren't reaching the scored run — calibration aborts. Infeasible corners are inconclusive, not a failure.

◆ wrote a file — but not the one the run reads
